title: introduce-sentinel-rollout-guard-for-latency-and-throughput-drift
author: Lena Park
description: Context and motivation: We need a lightweight automated guard between the continuous performance canary pipeline and the rollout controller to prevent upward rollouts from progressing when subtle latency or throughput drift is detected. This PR introduces 'Sentinel', a microservice and library hook that continuously evaluates per-deployment latency and throughput against adaptive baselines and issues 'pause' or 'rollback' signals to the rollout orchestrator. Key capabilities: adaptive baseline calculation (EWMA with decay + percentile windows), rate-aware thresholds (thresholds scale with qps), outlier suppression for short-lived spikes, a short circuit for cold-starts, and a sliding-window A/B drift comparator for canary vs baseline. This is intended to complement existing canary detectors by adding an application-aware, deployment-scoped guard that integrates with our rollout API. What changed (high level): added sentinel service and API, rollout controller integration points, a minimal sidecar adapter for legacy workloads, e2e smoke tests and a small local load generator for reproducible repros, observability dashboards and alert rules, docs and runbook, and a migration path to opt-in. Details: The sentinel service ingests time-series summaries from our metrics pipeline (latency p50/p95/p99, request rate, error rate) and runs a configurable detector algorithm. When the detector exceeds its policy for N consecutive windows the service emits an action to the rollout controller; actions are idempotent and annotated with causal metrics. Policies are configurable per-team via the rollout config. Rollout behavior: pause the rollout, open a ticket via webhook (optional), optionally trigger an automatic rollback to the last healthy revision if configured. Tests and validation: unit tests for detector logic, integration test exercising sentinel-controller handshake, canary e2e that simulates a latency regression and verifies a pause-and-rollback sequence, and a backfill tool to validate historic baselines. Backwards compatibility: Sentinel is opt-in per-deployment; default rollout policies remain unchanged until teams enable the guard. Migration notes are in docs/ops/sentinel.md. Checklist: - [x] detector library and service - [x] rollout controller hooks and API changes - [x] sidecar adapter for legacy endpoints - [x] e2e smoke tests and load generator - [x] dashboards and alerting - [x] docs and runbook - [x] release notes and feature flag gating Rollout strategy and migration: feature gated behind 'enable_sentinel' rollout flag; will be rolled out to internal tenants first then to customers by opt-in. Monitoring: new Grafana dashboard and a Prometheus alert that fires when sentinel issues a halt. Security: sentinel only reads aggregated metrics and uses existing metric read RBAC roles; no customer PII is ingested. Performance: sentinel runs as a single small binary with bounded memory; detector latency is sub-50ms per evaluation in our bench. Rationale for differences vs existing detectors: sentinel emphasizes adaptive baselines and rate-aware thresholds to reduce false positives on high QPS tails, and it integrates directly with the rollout controller to enable automated rollback, not just alerting. Merge metadata: merged via squash.

release_notes: Add 'Sentinel' rollout guard: an opt-in service to automatically pause or rollback rollouts on sustained latency or throughput drift. Configurable per-rollout and namespace-level opt-out available. No breaking changes. See docs/ops/sentinel.md for migration and tuning guidance.
